html:
SMTO-EML-0025 — SMTO can't find the sign-in setup for this email sender

GUID: 24dba33b-d03f-5a5f-853c-3e5a524d441f
Slug: email-auth-configuration-missing
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • This sender signs in through your email provider's approval screen (OAuth), but a saved sign-in entry it relies on is missing. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store, select the sender, open Value, select Reveal & edit value, and note the name in auth_ref. That is the name of the saved sign-in connection the sender expects to find.
  2. Search Parameter Store for that name. If it's missing, create it from an Email OAuth Connection template, or change auth_ref to a connection you have, and select Save. The sender can't sign in when the connection it names doesn't exist.
  3. Open that connection entry and check that its client_ref names a saved app entry that exists. If not, create one from the matching Email OAuth App template and select Save. The connection also needs its app entry; if either one is missing, this error appears.
  4. Ask SMTO in a conversation to connect the email account, then to test the connection. Connecting gets your provider's approval so SMTO can sign in and send.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the sender's sign-in status, such as ready or authorization required, instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who set up email sign-in for SMTO. Don't delete the sender to start over; fix or recreate only the missing sign-in entry.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OAuth2 connection named by the sender's auth.auth_ref, or the OAuth2 client named by that connection's client_ref, does not exist in Parameter Store.

What this means

  • A referenced OAuth connection or client configuration is missing. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • An OAuth connection or client reference cannot be resolved.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Look up auth.auth_ref (canonical key) in Parameter Store, then the connection record's client_ref. Create the missing oauth2_connection or oauth2_client record, or correct the reference, then run email.connect followed by email.connection_status.
  • Restore or select the referenced OAuth connection and client profiles before testing authorization.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • Both referenced authorization profiles exist and validate.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
